 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 03.02.2018 passed in MVC.No.165/2017 by the learned Senior CIvil Judge and AMACT, Shorapur (for short 'the Tribunal').
2.
Though this appeal is listed for admission, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. Heard on admission.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submits that the tribunal has committed an errror by not considering the contributory negligence between the motorycle and insured Mahindra Car.

The tribunal has assessed the disability at 57% by overlooking the fact that the petitioner has not examined treated doctors of United Hospital, Kalaburagi i.e., Neuro Surgeon,
Orthopedic Surgeon instead examined Dr.Kothari, who is General Surgeon and not competent doctor to assess the disability.
Hence, the tribunal has awarded the higher compensation.
On these grounds sought for allowing of the appeal.
5. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No1/petitioner supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
Hence, prays to dismiss the appeal.

6. I have perused the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal wherein at paragraph Nos.11 to 13 the tribunal has observed as under;
11.
The petitioner in order to prove his case got examined himself as PW1 and got examined two witness on his behalf as PW2 &PW3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P1 to 11.

PW1 has reiterated the petition averments in the affidavit of examination and relied upon the certified copy of FIR in crime No.55/2017, related charge sheet, MVI reports , wound certificate which are marked at Ex.P1 to 4.
Per contra respondent No 1 lead their side evidence and marked ExR1 to 3.

However having heard the arguments of all the counsels on perusal of Ex.P2 the charge sheet, it reveals that,
the said accident is caused due to sole negligence of the offending vehicle Mahindra Scorpio driver only.
Accordingly the driver of said vehicle has been alleged with the commission of offence punishable under Secs.279,337 338, of Indian Penal Code & U/Sec 187 of MV Act.

These documentary evidences are supported by the oral evidence of the petitioner and no worth has been elicited during his 6 MVC No.165/2017 crossexamination by the respondents counsels in order to disbelieve the version of the petitioner regarding the negligence of driver of the offending vehicle in occurrence of this accident.

Further the 2nd respondent's contention that, the rider of petitioner did not possess valid and effective Driving Licence on the date of accident, in this regard perusal of the Ex. P2 ChargeSheet reveals that the rider of petitioner has not ChargeSheeted with any offence . And the respondent No 2 has not led their documentary evidence to show that the driver of petitioner 's rider did not possess valid Driving Licence on the date of accident except bare contentions taken in the written statement .

In the result, I answer Point No 1 in the affirmative and Point No 2 in the National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Baramreddy And Anr on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967744/
2 negative.

sentences.text: 12. POINT No.3:
In this case the petitioner has sought the compensation of Rs. 46,60,000/ from the respondents for the injuries sustained by him in the road accident.
But the same has been opposed as excessive, baseless and exorbitant by the respondent No.1and 2 .

In this connection, in support of his oral evidence he has placed the wound certificate, Discharge card medical bills ,Disability certificates , X ray report , X ray films 7 MVC No.165/2017 statement of petitioner and Re statement of complainant Disability certificates Pointed by Dr . Rajendra Kothari and Dr. V.M Ghavalakar ,
Disability certificate as per Ex.P7.
In support of these documents he got examined the Doctor as PW2 who Pointed the disability certificate which is as per Ex.P7.
He has been elaborately crossexamined by the 2 nd respondent's counsel and denied his report as false and favorable,

Further the respondent No 1 counsel also adopted the crossexamination of Respondent No 2 but no worth has been elicited in order to disbelieve the clinical examination before arriving to conclusion to report regarding disability.

In the disability certificate which is as per Ex.P7 PW 2 Dr Rajendra Khotari has reported permanent disability of 37% whole body and PW 3 Dr. V. M Ghavalakar has reported 20% disablement to the whole body regarding brain injury and right upper limb respectively ,
Thus totally disablement of petitioner is 57% to the whole body.

13. According to the wound certificate, the petitioner has been recorded with grievous injuries and which could been seen from the XRay report and XRay films for which PW2 & PW 3 have recorded the permanent disability to an extent of 37% and MVC No.165/2017 20% to the whole body.

On consideration of all the probabilities in the affect of injuries sustained by the petitioner the given disability certificates are found proper and no counter evidence has been led by respondent No.1 and 2 in order to disbelieve their reports.
As such, I applied 57% permanent disability to determine the compensation.
In this case, the petitioner has contended that, he is aged about 30 years at the time of accident and he was earning about Rs.15000/ PM .
As such his own documents like wound certificate at Ex.P4 is containing his age as 30 years.
Thepetitioner is doing coolie work .
Therefore I applied his probable age as 30 years for the purpose of determination of compensation.

Therefore,
on consideration of the probabilities of earnings at the age of 30 years the notional income of Rs.6,000/ could be applied as a income of the petitioner that would be possible to earn from any avocation.
As such, I applied notional income of Rs.6,000/ per month for determination of the compensation.
On this basis, I proceed to determine the compensation.
According to the above said factors adopted by me the yearly income of petitioner will be at Rs.72,000/.
Then the loss of his future income to an extent of 57% permanent disability will be at Rs.41,040/.
According to Sarala Varma case the multiplier 17 is applied for the age of 30 years.
As such, the petitioner will be put into loss of future income to the tune of Rs.6,97,680/.
Therefore, he is entitled for the compensation of Rs.6,97,680/ towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability to an extent of 57%.

In addition to it, it is fit and proper to grant Rs.30,000/ towards loss of amenities, Rs.50,000/
towards pain & sufferings on account of two grievous injuries.
As revealed from the wound certificate as per Ex.P4, the petitioner is entitled medical bills at Ex.P6 Rs.1,52,992/ towards medical expenses.
According to discharge card at Ex.P5 the petitioner is found to be inpatient for 13 days for which he is entitled Rs.2600/ for food and nourishment charges and Rs.2600/ towards attendants charges.
Thus, in total the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 9,35,872/.

In order to avoid fraction this amount is rounded into Rs.9,36,000/ to grant with interest at the rate of National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Baramreddy And Anr on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190967744/

7. A perusal of the impugned judgment, I do not find any legal infirmities in the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
Hence, the tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record and passed the judgment and award in accordance with law and facts.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following;
 ORDER (a) The appeal is dismissed.
(b) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the tribunal forthwith.
